title: Jacob's ladder (Genesis 28:10–22)
hookLine: asleep on a stone, he dreams of angels going up and down
tomorrow: seven years like a few days

cards: Jacob is alone on the road with nothing. Esau is furious, and says he'll kill his brother once their father dies, so Rebekah sends Jacob away, to her brother Laban in Haran.

The quiet one who stayed in the tents now has no family, no flocks, no plan. The sun goes down. In the old JPS translation: "And he lighted upon the place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set."

Not a town, not an inn: just the place where it got dark. He puts stones under his head and lies down. Anyone who has spent a night in an airport, a hospital waiting room or a strange bed knows that place.

teach.h: A LADDER FROM EARTH TO HEAVEN.
teach.b: "And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it." Notice the order: ascending, then descending.

teach.h: UP FIRST: A CHANGE OF GUARD.
teach.b: You'd expect angels to come down from heaven first.
Rashi, the medieval commentator, explains: the angels who had guarded Jacob in the land of Israel were going up, their shift over, and new angels, for the road ahead, were coming down.
A changing of the guard over a sleeping man. Then God stands beside him and promises the land, children like the dust of the earth, and "I am with thee, and will keep thee whithersoever thou goest."
Jacob wakes and says: "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." He was sure he was nowhere. He was at the gate of heaven.
He names the spot Beth-el, the house of God.
In later Hebrew, HaMakom, the Place, becomes one of the names for God.

teach.h: SURELY THE LORD IS IN THIS PLACE.
teach.b: A midrash explains: God is the place of the world, and the world is not God's place. And the Talmud passage we met with Isaac says that Jacob, lighting on the place at nightfall, began the evening prayer.
In that view, the set is complete: Abraham the morning, Isaac the afternoon, Jacob the night. Jacob lay down in the middle of nowhere, and woke up saying God had been there all along.

how: Jews read Jacob's dream in the Torah portion Vayetze; tradition credits Jacob with the evening prayer, Maariv, and HaMakom, the Place, is used as a name for God, as in the words said to comfort mourners.

o: a dream of angels on a stairway, earth to heaven
a ladder of good deeds that lifts you to heaven
a stairway Jacob climbed to reach God's throne

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: Rashi: a changing of the guard
the Place, a name for God

s: in the dream, the angels come down first and then go up
the verse says ascending and descending. Rashi reads it as one guard going up and another coming down.
Jacob named the place Beth-el, house of God
he woke and said, surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.
the Talmud links Jacob to the evening prayer
Abraham the morning, Isaac the afternoon, Jacob the evening.

games.q: you're Jacob, alone, running from your brother. the sun has set and there's no town. what do you do?
o: lie down right there with a stone under your head.
games.why: he lights upon the place, sleeps on the ground, and dreams of a ladder to heaven. he wakes and says, I knew it not.

practice: Notice exactly where you are right now, this room, this car, this bed, and rest your eyes on one ordinary thing in it: a wall, a cup, a patch of floor.
If you pray, you can say Jacob's words silently: surely the LORD is in this place, and I knew it not; if not, just give this place your full attention, the way you would a place that mattered.
You don't have to feel anything special.
